extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of political philosophy; theorists and lawmakers interested in sovereignty and punishment
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts Hobbes' criteria and distinctions about the nature and legitimacy of punishment, types of punishments and rewards, and the causes of a commonwealth's dissolution as given in Leviathan (Chapters on Punishment and Dissolution).

rubrics_metrics.name: Origin of the Right or Authority of Punishing
rubrics_metrics.description: The Right which the Common-wealth (that is, he, or they that represent it) hath to Punish, is not grounded on any concession, or gift of the Subjects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes argues the sovereign's right to punish arises from the natural right each person had before commonwealth (right to all things for self-preservation) which is retained and strengthened when subjects lay down their own rights; therefore punishment is the sovereign's exercise of his own retained right, limited only by natural law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private Injuries and Revenges No Punishments
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither private revenges, nor injuries of private men, can properly be stiled Punishment; because they proceed not from publique Authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only harm inflicted by public authority counts as punishment; individual revenge is an act of hostility and not a legitimate punitive act under the commonwealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nor Denyall Of Preferment
rubrics_metrics.description: To be neglected, and unpreferred by the publique favour, is not a Punishment; because no new evill is thereby on any man Inflicted; he is onely left in the estate he was in before.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Loss of favor or preferment alone does not constitute punishment since it inflicts no new evil.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nor Pain Inflicted Without Publique Hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: The evill inflicted by publique Authority, without precedent publique condemnation, is not to be stiled by the name of Punishment; but of an hostile act;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punishment must follow public judgment/condemnation for the act to be properly called punishment; summary harm without trial is hostility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nor Pain Inflicted By Usurped Power
rubrics_metrics.description: The evill inflicted by usurped power, and Judges without Authority from the Soveraign, is not Punishment; but an act of hostility;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acts by usurped or illegitimate authority are not punishments because they do not emanate from the sovereign public authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nor Pain Inflicted Without Respect To The Future Good
rubrics_metrics.description: All evill which is inflicted without intention, or possibility of disposing the Delinquent, or (by his example) other men, to obey the Lawes, is not Punishment; but an act of hostility;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A key purpose of punishment is to induce future obedience (deterrence or reform); harm lacking that aim is not legitimate punishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturall Evill Consequences, No Punishments
rubrics_metrics.description: Hurt which is annexed by Nature to certain actions (e.g., being slain or wounded in assault, falling into sickness by unlawful act) is not contained in the name of Punishment in respect of men;
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Natural consequences or divine punishments differ from human (public) punishments because they are not inflicted by human authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hurt Inflicted, If Lesse Than The Benefit Of Transgressing, Is Not Punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: If the harm inflicted be lesse than the benefit, or contentment that naturally followeth the crime committed, that harm is not within the definition; and is rather the Price, or Redemption, than the Punishment of a Crime:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punishment must deter; if the penalty is less than the gain from the offense it fails as punishment and functions merely as a cost of the offense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where The Punishment Is Annexed To The Law, A Greater Hurt Is Not Punishment, But Hostility
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Punishment be determined and prescribed in the Law itself, and after the crime committed, there be a greater Punishment inflicted, the excesse is not Punishment, but an act of hostility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceeding a legally prescribed penalty transforms the act into hostility; conversely, where no penalty is prescribed any inflicted harm has the nature of punishment (i.e., arbitrary punishment is possible when law is silent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hurt Inflicted For A Fact Done Before The Law, No Punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Harm inflicted for a Fact done before there was a Law that forbad it, is not Punishment, but an act of Hostility: For before the Law, there is no transgression of the Law:
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retroactive punishment is illegitimate because punishment presupposes an existing law and judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Representative Of The Common-wealth Unpunishable
rubrics_metrics.description: Hurt inflicted on the Representative of the Common-wealth, is not Punishment, but an act of Hostility: Because ... Punishment is to be inflicted by publique Authority, which is the Authority only of the Representative it self.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The sovereign (or its representative) cannot be legitimately punished by the commonwealth because punishment must be public authority acting upon someone subject to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hurt To Revolted Subjects Is Done By Right Of War, Not By Way Of Punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Harme inflicted upon one that is a declared enemy, fals not under the name of Punishment: ... all the Harmes that can be done them, must be taken as acts of Hostility. But in declared Hostility, all infliction of evill is lawfull.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rebels who renounce subjection are treated as enemies; harms against them are acts of war rather than punishments of subjects and may be unlimited by prior penal law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of Punishments: Divine and Humane
rubrics_metrics.description: The first, and most generall distribution of Punishments, is into Divine, and Humane.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Divine punishments (to be discussed elsewhere) differ from humane (human) punishments which are commanded by man and further subdivided (see following types).

rubrics_metrics.name: Humane Punishments: Categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Humane punishments ... are either Corporall, or Pecuniary, or Ignominy, or Imprisonment, or Exile, or mixt of these.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hobbes enumerates the substantive categories by which human punishments are legitimately administered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punishments Corporall
rubrics_metrics.description: Corporall Punishment is that, which is inflicted on the body directly, and according to the intention of him that inflicteth it: such as are stripes, or wounds, or deprivation of such pleasures of the body, as were before lawfully enjoyed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes intentional bodily pain or deprivation of bodily pleasures; Hobbes clarifies scope and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capitall and Less-than-Capitall Distinction
rubrics_metrics.description: Capitall, is the Infliction of Death; and that either simply, or with torment. Lesse than Capitall, are Stripes, Wounds, Chains, and any other corporall Paine, not in its own nature mortall.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If death occurs unintentionally as an accident of punishment, it is not to be esteemed capital because intention matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pecuniary Punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Pecuniary Punishment, is that which consisteth not only in the deprivation of a Summe of Mony, but also of Lands, or any other goods ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a law that levies money is designed to gather revenue it may be a 'price of privilege' rather than punishment, except when tied to natural or religious law; payments to injured parties are satisfaction extinguishing accusation but not the offender's crime.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ignominy
rubrics_metrics.description: Ignominy, is the infliction of such Evill, as is made Dishonorable; or the deprivation of such Good, as is made Honourable by the Common-wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguishes natural honors (courage, wisdom) which cannot be taken by law from honors created by commonwealth (titles, badges, offices) which can be revoked as punishment (e.g., degradation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Imprisonment
rubrics_metrics.description: Imprisonment, is when a man is by publique Authority deprived of liberty; and may happen from two divers ends ... one is the safe custody of a man accused; the other is the inflicting of paine on a man condemned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-trial restraint for custody is not punishment; post-conviction confinement as pain is punishment. Excessive pre-hearing restraint beyond necessary custody violates natural law. 'Imprisonment' covers houses, islands, forced labour, chains, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exile (Banishment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exile ... is when a man is for a crime, condemned to depart out of the dominion of the Common-wealth ... and seemeth not in its own nature, without other circumstances, to be a Punishment; but rather an escape, or a publique commandement to avoid Punishment by flight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exile alone (mere change of air) is not always punishment unless coupled with loss of goods; exile with deprivation of goods is in effect pecuniary punishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punishment Of Innocent Subjects Is Contrary To The Law Of Nature
rubrics_metrics.description: All Punishments of Innocent subjects, be they great or little, are against the Law of Nature; For Punishment is only of Transgression of the Law, and therefore there can be no Punishment of the Innocent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punishing innocents violates natural law, is unjust, ingratitude, and breaches equity (equal distribution of justice).

rubrics_metrics.name: But The Harme Done To Innocents In War, Not So
rubrics_metrics.description: The Infliction of what evill soever, on an Innocent man, that is not a Subject, if it be for the benefit of the Common-wealth, and without violation of any former Covenant, is no breach of the Law of Nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In wartime or against those who are not subjects (or have renounced subjection), harming innocents may be lawful as part of war; rebels can lawfully suffer harms extended even to posterity because rebellion is relapse into war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reward, Is Either Salary, Or Grace
rubrics_metrics.description: REWARD, is either of Gift, or by Contract. When by Contract, it is called Salary, and Wages; ... When of Gift, it is benefit proceeding from the Grace of them that bestow it...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Salaries (contractual rewards) obligate performance in justice; gifts (grace) bind only honour and gratitude; soldiers may demand wages as debt; sovereign appointments create different obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benefits Bestowed For Fear, Are Not Rewards
rubrics_metrics.description: The benefits which a Soveraign bestoweth on a Subject, for fear of some power, and ability he hath to do hurt to the Common-wealth, are not properly Rewards; ... but are rather Sacrifices ... and encourage not to obedience, but ... extortion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gifts made out of fear of extortion are not legitimate rewards and undermine obedience by encouraging further extortion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salaries Certain And Casuall
rubrics_metrics.description: Some Salaries are certain, and proceed from the publique Treasure; and others uncertain, and casuall, proceeding from the execution of the Office for which the Salary is ordained; the later is in some cases hurtfull to the Common-wealth; as in the case of Judicature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Casual salaries for judges (fees per suit) incentivize litigation and jurisdictional competition; offices of execution do not share those disadvantages because their work cannot be increased by self-interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissolution Of Common-wealths Proceedeth From Imperfect Institution
rubrics_metrics.description: When Common-wealths are dissolved by intestine disorder the fault is ... in the Makers, and orderers of them. Infirmities arise from Imperfect Institution, resembling diseases of a natural body from Defectuous Procreation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A properly constituted commonwealth should aim to last; defects in foundational structure cause internal decay and dissolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Want Of Absolute Power
rubrics_metrics.description: That a man to obtain a Kingdome, is sometimes content with lesse Power, than to the Peace, and defence of the Common-wealth is necessarily required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Insufficient sovereign power or voluntary limits can enable rebellion and foreign interference; lack of necessary authority undermines state's ability to preserve peace and defend itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Private Judgement Of Good and Evill
rubrics_metrics.description: That every private man is Judge of Good and Evill actions ... the measure of Good and Evill actions, is the Civill Law; and the Judge the Legislator, who is alwayes Representative of the Common-wealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowing private individuals to judge laws leads to debate, selective obedience, and disorder; civil law must be the public measure of good and evil.

rubrics_metrics.name: Erroneous Conscience
rubrics_metrics.description: Whatsoever a man does against his Conscience, is Sinne; and it dependeth on the presumption of making himself judge of Good and Evill. ... the Conscience may be erroneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Private conscience can err; treating every action against conscience as sin undermines civil obedience because law is the public conscience for subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretence Of Inspiration
rubrics_metrics.description: Faith and Sanctity, are not to be attained by study and reason, but by supernaturall Inspiration ... which ... would make private men judges and undermine civil law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims of supernatural inspiration that place personal revelation above civil law threaten civil authority and can dissolve government by encouraging private judgments and prophetic claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subjecting The Soveraign Power To Civill Lawes
rubrics_metrics.description: That he that hath the Soveraign Power, is subject to the Civill Lawes. ... To be subject to Lawes, is to be subject to the Common-wealth ... which is not subjection, but freedome from the Lawes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Making sovereign subject to civil laws effectively sets another judge or sovereign above him, leading to perpetual cycles of competing sovereigns and dissolution of commonwealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attributing Of Absolute Propriety To The Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: That every private man has an absolute Propriety in his Goods; such, as excludeth the Right of the Soveraign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If subjects claim absolute property excluding sovereign's rights, the sovereign cannot perform protections and the commonwealth cannot function; subjects' proprietorship derives from sovereign's protection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dividing Of The Soveraign Power
rubrics_metrics.description: That the Soveraign Power may be divided. For what is it to divide the Power of a Common-wealth, but to Dissolve it; for Powers divided mutually destroy each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Division of sovereign power creates multiple competing sovereigns/factions and destroys unity necessary for a functioning commonwealth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation Of Neighbour Nations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Example of different Government in a neighbouring Nation, disposeth men to alteration of the forme already setled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Admiring or imitating neighbouring governments can provoke attempts to change one's own regime and risk instability; proximity of successful alternatives fuels desire for novelty and change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imitation Of The Greeks And Romans
rubrics_metrics.description: Reading the books of Policy, and Histories of the antient Greeks, and Romans ... leads some to imagine popular forms produce liberty and monarchies slavery, prompting rebellion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Romanticizing ancient republics (or their accounts) without sober reason fosters sedition and mistaken beliefs about the causes of historical success, risking upheaval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict Between Ghostly (Spiritual) and Civill Power
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Civill Power, and the Power of the Common-wealth is the same thing; and that Supremacy, and the Power of making Canons, and granting Faculties, implyeth a Common-wealth; it followeth, that where one is Soveraign, another Supreme ... there must needs be two Common-wealths, of one & the same Subjects
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concurrent claims of ecclesiastical (ghostly) authority and civil authority create two kingdoms over the same subjects, inciting civil war and dissolution; one must be subordinate to preserve unity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixt Government As Division
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Power of levying mony has depended on a generall Assembly; the Power of conduct and command on one man; and the Power of making Lawes on another, this endangereth the Common-wealth ... it is not one independent Common-wealth, but three independent Factions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mixed government that splits core sovereign faculties across bodies effectively divides the commonwealth into factions; such bifurcation undermines consent, nourishment (resources), and coherent action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Want Of Mony
rubrics_metrics.description: Difficulty of raising Mony for the necessary uses of the Common-wealth ... ariseth from the opinion, that every Subject hath of a Propriety in his lands and goods, exclusive of the Soveraigns Right to the use of the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inability to secure funds due to subjects' sense of exclusive property forces sovereign to resort to legal stratagems or violent measures, weakening state capacity and potentially causing demise.
